current: Meaning inversion — label by EFFECT, not by surface form. If an error's effect is to reverse the reference's polarity (negation), direction, quantity or degree, or agent/recipient (who does what to whom), report it as subtype {mi}, whatever its surface form: a preposition swap, a word-choice swap or a dropped word. A negator (not, no, never…) that the learner dropped or added so that the polarity reverses is {mi}, not {om} or {ad}. Content that is lost without any such reversal stays {om}. A change of degree that does not reverse it (very → quite) is not an inversion. {co} is only for a sentence that contradicts itself, visible from the learner text alone without the reference; a clash with the reference is {mi}. The severity of {mi} is always critical (2).
proposed: Meaning inversion — label by EFFECT, not by surface form. Use subtype {mi} for any error whose effect is to reverse the reference's polarity (negation), direction, quantity or degree (more → less, always → never), or who does what to whom — whatever its surface form: a preposition swap, a different word, or a dropped or added word. In particular, a negator (not, no, never …) that the learner dropped or added so that the polarity reverses belongs here, not under {om} or {ad}. Report such an error once, under this subtype only — never also under its surface-form type. Content that is lost without any reversal stays an omission, and a change of degree that does not reverse it (very → quite) is not an inversion. {co} is only for a sentence that contradicts itself or links its clauses illogically, visible from the learner text alone; a reversal that only shows when compared with the reference is a meaning inversion. A meaning inversion is always severity critical (2).
reason: Three problems. (1) 'a clash with the reference is {mi}' is far too broad: almost every error is a clash with the reference, so a literal-minded grader could file wrong words, omissions etc. as inversions. It must say a REVERSAL visible only against the reference. (2) The {co} sentence drops the definition's second limb (a connective asserting the wrong logical relation, because/although), so it now contradicts the contradiction gloss shown in the same prompt. (3) Each placeholder expands to its full gloss: {mi} appears 4x, {om} 2x, and the rendered en Verifier block is ~750 words of nested parentheses. The rewrite uses each placeholder exactly once (still fills {mi}/{om}/{ad}/{co}; no new fields) and adds the definition's 'never tag both' rule, which the en block lacked. Severity index 2 = critical is correct (SEVERITY_ENUM). zh/ja blocks likely share issue (1)/(3) — native reviewers should check.
